detect_client_side_authz_gate: Enforce the same authorization decision server-side on every request the gated action triggers; treat the client-side flag purely as a UI hint, never as the sole gate. Verify the backend independently checks the user's role/entitlement on the endpoint itself, not just a client-supplied flag or session field.
detect_angular_bypass_security_trust: Avoid bypassSecurityTrust* wherever the value can be influenced by user input, server data, or config; let Angular's DomSanitizer perform its default escaping. If a bypass is unavoidable (e.g. a known-safe embed URL), restrict it to a compile-time constant or a value validated against a strict allowlist before the call.
detect_ajax_header_manipulation: Never use a URL/query-string value to select or build the name of an outgoing header. Whitelist a small fixed set of header names in code and validate header values against what the backend expects; reject any header name/value pair a client tries to set from user-controlled input.
detect_cookie_manipulation_url_param: Don't write raw URL-derived data into document.cookie. If a cookie must reflect a URL parameter, validate it against an allowlist and always encode the value with encodeURIComponent before assignment; set cookie attributes (Path, Domain, SameSite, Secure) explicitly in code rather than letting attacker input control them via injected `;` separators.
detect_dom_setattribute_url_param: Never pass a URL-derived value as the value of setAttribute for src/href/style/srcdoc/action/formaction/background/poster/data. Validate against an allowlist of protocols/paths, or run the value through a dedicated sanitizer (a URL sanitizer that rejects javascript: schemes, or DOMPurify for HTML/style content) before the DOM write.
detect_storage_manipulation_url_param: Treat localStorage/sessionStorage as an untrusted-input sink when values originate from the URL. Validate/allowlist the value before persisting it, and never render a previously stored value back into the DOM without escaping — persistence makes an unvalidated write far more dangerous than a one-off reflected sink.
detect_websocket_url_poisoning: Don't let a URL parameter determine the WebSocket endpoint. Hardcode the WebSocket host/path in code or resolve it from a trusted, server-controlled configuration value; if a dynamic room/channel name is required, validate it against a strict allowlist before building the URL.
detect_css_injection_style_sink: Never interpolate a URL-derived value directly into style.cssText, a style attribute, or a CSS-in-JS template. Map user input to a fixed set of known- safe values (e.g. theme names mapped to pre-defined CSS classes) instead of passing raw attacker-controlled text into any CSS sink — CSS injection can exfiltrate data even without script execution.
detect_js_injection_eval: Remove eval/new Function/string-based setTimeout/setInterval entirely — use direct function references or JSON.parse for data. There is essentially never a legitimate reason to feed URL-derived text into any of these on the client; refactor to avoid dynamic code execution altogether.
detect_insecure_random_token_storage: Replace Math.random() with a cryptographically secure generator (crypto.getRandomValues() or crypto.randomUUID()) for any value used as a session identifier, CSRF token, or other security-sensitive token before persisting it to cookies or Web Storage.
detect_link_manipulation_href: Validate any URL-derived value before assigning it to an element's href; reject javascript: and data: schemes and allow only http(s) URLs or relative paths, via an allowlist check or a URL-sanitizing helper applied at the point of assignment.
detect_open_redirect_url_param: Never navigate directly to a URL-derived value. Validate the destination against an allowlist of known internal paths/origins before calling location.href/assign/replace or window.open; reject anything that doesn't match rather than trying to blocklist dangerous schemes.
detect_cspt_fetch_url_param: URL-encode any URL-derived value with encodeURIComponent before interpolating it into a fetch() URL path segment, so `../` and other path- traversal characters can't redirect the request to a different endpoint. Prefer passing user input as a query parameter rather than a path segment where possible.
detect_cspt_xhr_url_param: URL-encode any URL-derived value with encodeURIComponent before interpolating it into an XHR/axios request URL's path segment, and prefer query parameters over path segments for user-controlled values to avoid path traversal reaching a different API route.
detect_postMessage: No fix needed for the listener by itself — this rule is informational. Ensure any postMessage listener validates event.origin with an exact-match allowlist and never trusts the message payload/source without validation.
detect_postMessage_function_href: Validate event.origin against an exact-match allowlist before the handler runs, and never assign postMessage-derived data directly to `.href` — validate it against an allowlist of expected values/paths first.
detect_postMessage_innerHtml_sink: Validate event.origin against an exact-match allowlist before the handler runs, and never assign postMessage-derived data directly to innerHTML — sanitize with DOMPurify or use textContent instead.
detect_postMessage_wildcard_origin: Replace the wildcard `"*"` target origin with the specific expected origin of the receiving window, so the browser refuses to deliver the message to any other origin.
detect_postmessage_eval: Remove the eval() call from the message handler entirely, and always validate event.origin against an exact allowlist of trusted origins before processing any postMessage payload. Never execute message data as code under any circumstances.
detect_postmessage_weak_origin_check: Replace substring-based origin checks (endsWith/includes/indexOf/startsWith) with an exact string-equality comparison against one or more fully-qualified allowed origins, e.g. `event.origin === "https://trusted.example.com"`.
detect_prototype_pollution_merge_gadget: Filter out __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys before merging parsed JSON into another object (or use a dedicated safe-merge utility that blocks these keys, or `Object.create(null)` as the merge target), or switch to `structuredClone`/a plain deep-copy that doesn't touch the prototype chain.
detect_redos_url_param: Never build a RegExp pattern directly from URL-derived input. If dynamic matching against user input is required, escape all regex metacharacters first (e.g. lodash's escapeRegExp) so the value can only match literally, not act as a pattern.
detect_dompurify_forcekeepattr_hook: Remove the forceKeepAttr assignment from sanitize hooks unless there is a specific, reviewed reason to bypass DOMPurify's attribute check for that one attribute; if it's needed, scope it as tightly as possible (single attribute, single tag) and keep DOMPurify updated to a patched version.
detect_non_global_regex_sanitizer: Add the global (`g`) flag to any regex used with `.replace()` as a sanitizer so all occurrences of the dangerous pattern are stripped, not just the first; better yet, use a maintained sanitization library (DOMPurify, sanitize-html) instead of hand-rolled regex stripping.
detect_cloud_credentials_in_bundle: Revoke and rotate the exposed credential immediately, then remove it from the client bundle entirely — cloud API keys/IAM credentials must never ship in frontend code. Move the operation behind an authenticated backend endpoint that holds the credential server-side, or use short-lived, scoped tokens issued per-session if client-side access is unavoidable.
detect_hardcoded_hmac_signing_key: Remove the hardcoded signing key from client code and move HMAC signing/verification to the server, where the key can stay secret. If the client only needs to verify a server-issued signature, have the server hand out a short-lived, scoped token instead of a static shared secret.
detect_hardcoded_secrets: Revoke and rotate the exposed secret immediately, then remove it from the bundle. Any credential intended for server-side use (Stripe secret keys, SendGrid/Slack tokens, webhook secrets, private keys) must be read from server-side environment/secret storage and never bundled into client- shipped JavaScript.
detect_dom_xss_dangerouslySetInnerHTML: Sanitize the HTML with DOMPurify (or an equivalent, actively-maintained sanitizer) immediately before passing it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML/v-html; avoid rendering raw server/response HTML unless a sanitization step sits directly in the render path.
detect_dom_xss_innerHTML_url_source: Don't write URL-derived data into innerHTML/outerHTML. Use `textContent` for plain text, or sanitize with DOMPurify if HTML content is genuinely required; never fall back to home-grown escaping.
detect_jquery_html_injection_url_param: Don't interpolate URL-derived values into the jQuery constructor or `.html()`. Use `.text()` for plain content, or sanitize with DOMPurify before calling `.html()` if markup is genuinely required.
detect_json_injection_to_dangerouslyseti: Treat any JSON.parse() result derived from URL/user input as untrusted before it reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML — sanitize the relevant HTML fields with DOMPurify, or render structured fields with React's normal escaping JSX bindings instead of raw HTML.
detect_react_createelement_dynamic_type: Never pass a URL-derived value as the `type` argument to React.createElement/createElement. Map user input to a component/tag through an explicit allowlist (a lookup object of permitted tag names) instead of using the raw value directly.
detect_regression_angular_directive_inne: Sanitize the value with DOMPurify before assigning it to nativeElement.innerHTML, or use Angular's built-in interpolation/[innerText] binding instead of a direct native DOM write.
detect_regression_angular_safe_html_pipe: Remove the bypassSecurityTrustHtml() call from the pipe; sanitize the value with DOMPurify (or accept Angular's default sanitization) before returning it as safe HTML.
detect_regression_cspt_fetch_react_docs: URL-encode the path parameter with encodeURIComponent before building the fetch() URL template literal, so `../` segments can't redirect the request to a different API route; check sibling components using the same fetch(`/api/route/${param}`) pattern too.
detect_regression_domparser_innerhtml: Sanitize the parsed document's body (e.g. with DOMPurify) before re- assigning its innerHTML to a live element — parsing into a detached DOM tree and re-serializing does not neutralize script/event-handler content.
detect_regression_dsih_react: Sanitize the content with DOMPurify before passing it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML's `__html` value.
detect_regression_dsih_react_adminposts: Sanitize the content with DOMPurify before passing it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML's `__html` value.
detect_regression_dynamic_prop_innerhtml: Sanitize the value before the bracket-notation assignment resolves to innerHTML/outerHTML at runtime — the dynamic property lookup doesn't change that this is still an HTML sink.
detect_regression_eval_react_debug: Remove the eval() call from the debug console entirely; if expression evaluation is genuinely needed for a dev tool, gate it behind a build flag that's stripped from production bundles, and never expose it to end users.
detect_regression_event_delegation_inner: Sanitize the data-attribute value with DOMPurify before writing it to innerHTML in the delegated click handler.
detect_regression_innerhtml_react_search: Sanitize search-result content with DOMPurify before the innerHTML assignment, or switch to React's normal text/JSX rendering instead of a direct DOM write.
detect_regression_intersection_observer_: Sanitize the lazy-loaded content with DOMPurify before assigning it to innerHTML inside the IntersectionObserver callback — deferring the write until the element is visible doesn't make the sink any safer.
detect_regression_new_function_urlparam: Remove the new Function() call built from a URL parameter entirely; there is no safe way to build executable code from user input on the client.
detect_regression_promise_chain_innerhtm: Sanitize the resolved value with DOMPurify immediately before the innerHTML write, regardless of how many .then() layers deep it occurs.
detect_regression_proto_pollution_innerh: Fix the prototype-pollution gadget by filtering __proto__/constructor/prototype keys on merge, and separately sanitize the value with DOMPurify before it reaches the innerHTML write — both steps in the chain need remediation.
detect_regression_settimeout_innerhtml: Sanitize the value with DOMPurify before the deferred innerHTML write inside the timer callback; wrapping the write in setTimeout doesn't change the fix.
detect_regression_vue_vhtml_computed: Sanitize the value (or fix the upstream computed-property transformation) before it's bound via v-html — a multi-step computed chain doesn't neutralize unescaped HTML at the end of it.
detect_regression_vue_watcher_innerhtml: Don't rely on a partial regex-based filter (e.g. stripping only `<script>` tags); sanitize the value with DOMPurify inside the watcher callback before writing it to innerHTML.
admin_api: Informational: confirm every endpoint under an admin path enforces server- side authentication and role-based authorization; don't rely on a non- obvious path alone as protection (security by obscurity).
api_path: Informational: no remediation required by itself — this classifies an endpoint as an API path. Ensure any endpoint identified this way has the correct authentication and authorization applied server-side.
missing_authorization_header: Add authentication to the endpoint: require and validate an Authorization header, API key, auth token, or session cookie server-side, and reject requests that are missing all of them.
